editorial.title: Read a chair-joint inspection
editorial.subtitle: A fictional field-note example about connecting an observation to its record.
editorial.disclaimer: Illustrative records and diagrams, not repair instructions or a safety assessment.

sections.title: Observe the gap
sections.text: Note A records a visible line at the rear rail joint. The diagram marks the observed location; it does not show movement or establish a cause. Keep the location and the observation together so the next reader can distinguish what was seen from what was inferred.
sections.caption: Figure 1. Original schematic: the numbered line marks the rear rail location described in Note A. It is deliberately enlarged for reading and is not a measured gap.
sections.note: Recorded observation: visible line at rear rail. Cause: unknown.

sections.title: Compare the record
sections.text: Note B shows the same location in a second drawing. The two drawings use matching labels, allowing the record to be compared without implying that an inspection or repair took place. A differently cropped picture would not by itself establish a change in condition.
sections.caption: Figure 2. Original schematic comparison with the same rear rail label. Both drawings are fictional artifacts; no before-and-after performance claim is made.
sections.note: Comparison limit: drawings share a label, not a measured inspection result.

sections.title: Record what remains unknown
sections.text: A useful note preserves the object location, the observed feature and its uncertainty. In this example the cause, dimensions and structural condition remain unknown. A reader can save this section as a reading place and return to its exact heading rather than treating completion of the article as approval of the object.
sections.note: Object: example chair. Location: rear rail. Feature: visible line. Cause and structural condition: unknown.

editorial.behavior: Navigate to each section with ordinary anchors and focus its heading. Save or replace a reading place for a section in local page memory, resume it, and clear it. Keep source note, artifact and caption associated with the section. No remote save, repair recommendation or fabricated outcome.
